title: Blind Bartimaeus
description: Blind Bartimaeus in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 4 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, first published in 1842. The tune, FILLMORE, is by Jeremiah Ingalls. This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Blind Bar_-ti-mae-us at the gates Of Jer-i-cho_ in dark-ness waits: He hears the crowd;_ he hears a breath say "It is Christ_ of Naz-a-reth!"_ And calls_ in tones of a-go-ny, "O Je-sus, Je_-sus pi-ty me!"

lines: He hears the crowd; he hears a breath
And calls in tones of agony,
But still, above the noisy crowd,
The blind man's cry is shrill and loud:
Then saith the Christ, as silent stands
The crowd, "What wilt thou at My hands?"
And he replies, "O give me light!
Rabbi, restore the blind man's sight."
Thy faith, thy faith hath savèd thee."
Ye that hath eyes and cannot see,
Recall those mighty voices three-"O Jesus,
"Thy faith, thy faith hath savèd thee."
